summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube for nutritional supplementation was admitted to the surgical service with one week of sharp left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back and worsened by oral intake and tube feeds. Initial evaluation included chest/abdominal radiographs and contrast assessment via G-tube without evidence of free air or extravasation. On hospital day 2, EGD demonstrated a single 10 mm gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer with otherwise normal post-bypass anatomy. She was treated with IV pantoprazole and sucralfate (oral and via G-tube) and underwent multiple tube-feeding adjustments due to pain intolerance; ultimately tube feeds were held and TPN was started via PICC (with radiographic confirmation of line position). CT abdomen/pelvis showed no obstruction or gastrogastric fistula but did note significant stool burden. A small supraumbilical pustule was drained and cultured, growing MRSA without systemic infection. Tube feeds were retrialed late in the course; TPN was discontinued and the PICC removed after improved tolerance on Peptamen Bariatric cycled at 60 mL/hr for 12 hours with scheduled water flushes. She was discharged home with services on liquid pantoprazole BID, sucralfate QID (oral and via G-tube), bowel regimen, pain control plan including increased bedtime nortriptyline, and close surgical and GI follow-up.
